name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
description: Adversaries may attempt to exploit vulnerabilities in Internet-facing software (web applications, APIs) to gain initial access. Common vectors include SQL Injection (SQLi), Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), and unauthenticated API flaws.
detection: Monitor application logs for database error responses (HTTP 500), SQL syntax tokens (UNION SELECT, OR 1=1), and abnormal query lengths. Inspect WAF and proxy logs for automated injection tools.
mitigation: Enforce parameterized queries (prepared statements), input validation, WAF filtering, and least-privilege database user permissions.

name: File and Directory Discovery
description: Adversaries may enumerate files and directories or exploit Path Traversal / Local File Inclusion (LFI) to read sensitive system configuration, application source code, or credentials (such as /etc/passwd, .env, or wp-config.php).
detection: Detect repeated directory traversal sequences (../, ..%2f), requests for hidden directories (/.git/, /.env), and attempts to load system files via web query parameters.
mitigation: Sanitize user-supplied file path parameters, disable directory browsing, restrict web server file system permissions using chroot or container isolation.

name: Brute Force: Password Guessing
description: Adversaries with no prior knowledge of passwords may attempt to guess credentials by systematically testing many common passwords against one or more user accounts (SSH, web login portals, API keys).
detection: Correlate rapid bursts of failed authentication attempts (SSH Failed password or HTTP 401/403) from a single IP address within a short timeframe.
mitigation: Enforce account lockouts or progressive delays, implement Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), rate-limit login endpoints, and deploy IP auto-banning (e.g., Fail2Ban).

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
description: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters to execute arbitrary commands on a host, commonly via web application OS command injection (using shell metacharacters ;, |, &&).
detection: Monitor web server child processes executing unexpected shell commands (cat /etc, whoami, nc, /bin/sh, ping -c) and inspect parameters for shell separators.
mitigation: Avoid invoking shell interpreters from application code, use strongly typed process execution APIs with fixed arguments, and run web services as unprivileged service accounts.

name: Active Scanning: Vulnerability Scanning
description: Adversaries may scan public infrastructure with automated tools (sqlmap, Nikto, Gobuster, DirBuster, Hydra) to find accessible paths, misconfigurations, and known vulnerabilities.
detection: Search web access logs for known automated vulnerability scanner User-Agent signatures and bursts of rapid 404/403 responses exploring non-existent endpoints.
mitigation: Block known malicious scanner User-Agents at the edge/reverse proxy, implement rate-limiting, and use threat intelligence IP reputation feeds.

name: Valid Accounts
description: Adversaries may obtain credentials through brute force, credential dumping, or phishing and use them to gain legitimate access to accounts, often blending in with normal user activity.
detection: Correlate successful logins immediately following bursts of authentication failures from the same source IP, or logins from unusual locations and times.
mitigation: Enforce MFA, monitor for impossible travel, and automatically reset passwords on accounts subjected to sustained brute force.

name: OS Credential Dumping
description: Adversaries may attempt to dump credentials from operating system files (e.g. /etc/shadow, SAM and SYSTEM registry hives) to obtain password hashes for offline cracking.
detection: Alert on web requests or file access attempts targeting /etc/shadow, SAM hives, or LSASS memory access.
mitigation: Restrict file permissions strictly to root/SYSTEM, enable host-based endpoint detection (EDR), and ensure credential files cannot be read by web processes.
